events.title: Pompey is murdered on landing in Egypt
events.description: Fleeing after Pharsalus, Pompey the Great was stabbed to death as he stepped ashore, on the orders of Ptolemy XIII's advisers. Caesar is said to have wept when shown his rival's head.
events.html: Fleeing after Pharsalus, Pompey the Great was stabbed to death as he stepped ashore, on the orders of Ptolemy XIII's advisers. Caesar is said to have wept when shown his rival's head.

events.title: Pope Pontian resigns and is exiled to the mines of Sardinia
events.description: Arrested during the persecution of Christians in the reign of the Emperor Maximinus Thrax, Pontian, bishop of Rome since 21 July 230, resigned his office. He was exiled to the mines of Sardinia together with the Christian writer Hippolytus of Rome.

events.title: Constantius II defeats the usurper Magnentius at Mursa
events.description: At Mursa, near the Via Militaris in the province of Pannonia, the eastern Roman armies of Emperor Constantius II defeated the western forces of the usurper Magnentius. One of the bloodiest battles in Roman history, it was a pyrrhic victory for Constantius.

events.title: Duke Wenceslaus I of Bohemia is murdered by his brother Boleslaus
events.description: Wenceslaus I, Prince of Bohemia since 921, was murdered by nobles led by his younger brother Boleslaus, who became duke in his place. The year was probably 935, though 929 is also given.

events.title: William of Normandy lands at Pevensey
events.description: William's invasion fleet landed unopposed on the Sussex coast while King Harold was in the north. Just over two weeks later William won the Battle of Hastings.
events.html: William's invasion fleet landed unopposed on the Sussex coast while King Harold was in the north. Just over two weeks later William won the Battle of Hastings.

events.title: Henry I of England defeats and captures Robert Curthose at Tinchebray
events.description: In Normandy, King Henry I of England defeated the Norman army of his elder brother Robert Curthose, Duke of Normandy, and captured him. Robert spent the rest of his life in captivity, and Henry reunited Normandy with England.
events.html: In Normandy, King Henry I of England defeated the Norman army of his elder brother Robert Curthose, Duke of Normandy, and captured him. Robert spent the rest of his life in captivity, and Henry reunited Normandy with England.

events.title: Louis IV defeats and captures Frederick the Fair at Mühldorf
events.description: Near Mühldorf am Inn, Louis IV of Bavaria defeated and captured his cousin and rival king Frederick the Fair of Austria. It is often described as one of the last great battles of mounted knights fought without firearms.
events.html: Near Mühldorf am Inn, Louis IV of Bavaria defeated and captured his cousin and rival king Frederick the Fair of Austria. It is often described as one of the last great battles of mounted knights fought without firearms.

events.title: American and French armies begin the siege of Yorktown
events.description: Washington and Rochambeau's forces closed in on Cornwallis at Yorktown, Virginia, while a French fleet blocked escape by sea. Cornwallis surrendered on 19 October, effectively ending the war.

events.title: Alexander Fleming notices the mould that leads to penicillin
events.description: Back from holiday, Alexander Fleming found a mould killing bacteria on a culture plate in his London laboratory. Developed into a drug in the 1940s, penicillin opened the antibiotic era.

events.title: Ferdinand Marcos dies in exile in Hawaii
events.description: Former Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos died in Honolulu, three years after the People Power Revolution drove him from power. His regime was notorious for martial law and plunder.
